repairs.failure_pattern: LightGBM training fails because categorical features are identified by column names while the supplied training matrix is a NumPy array without column metadata.
repair_steps: Determine whether the matrix passed to LightGBM preserves pandas column names.
If training from a NumPy array, map each categorical feature to its stable integer column index.
Pass those indices through the categorical_feature argument of lgb.Dataset instead of placing feature names in model parameters.
Alternatively, preserve the pandas DataFrame and use the LightGBM-supported name-based categorical feature syntax consistently.
Verify that categorical references resolve against the final post-transformation feature order before training.
repairs.root_cause: Converting a pandas feature frame to a NumPy array removes column names, so LightGBM cannot resolve name-based categorical_feature entries against the training matrix.
repairs.title: Provisional: Align LightGBM categorical references with the training matrix representation
repairs.when_to_use: Use when LightGBM reports that categorical_feature is not a number or cannot resolve categorical feature names, and the model input was converted to a NumPy array.

repairs.failure_pattern: Validation features contain fare aggregates computed from the full labeled dataset before the train-validation split.
repair_steps: Create the train-validation split before computing any fare-derived location statistics.
Fit the location aggregation table using only the training partition.
Join the frozen training-derived aggregates onto validation and test rows without recomputing them.
For training rows, use out-of-fold aggregates or leave-one-out logic when self-inclusion would materially leak the row target.
Define fallback values from training-partition statistics for unseen or sparse locations.
repairs.root_cause: Location-level mean, standard deviation, or count features derived from fare_amount include validation targets, allowing validation observations to influence their own predictors and producing an optimistically biased score.
repairs.title: Provisional: Fit target-derived location aggregates only from the training partition
repairs.when_to_use: Use when features aggregate fare_amount or another target by rounded coordinates, geographic cells, routes, or location clusters and validation is performed on a held-out partition.

repairs.failure_pattern: A numeric scaler is fitted on validation observations, either by concatenating train and validation data or by scaling the complete dataset before fold selection.
repair_steps: Create the temporal holdout or cross-validation fold indices before fitting the scaler.
Fit StandardScaler or the selected transformer only on numeric columns from the active training partition.
Use the fitted transformer without refitting to transform validation and test numeric columns.
Repeat scaler fitting independently for every cross-validation fold.
Keep categorical identifiers unscaled when the downstream model treats them as categorical features.
repairs.root_cause: The fitted means and variances incorporate the held-out distribution, violating validation isolation and biasing preprocessing toward data that should remain unseen.
repairs.title: Confirmed: Fit numeric scaling independently within each training partition
repairs.when_to_use: Use when validation or fold rows contribute to fit, fit_transform, or preprocessing statistics used by the corresponding training partition.

repairs.failure_pattern: Validation error grows rapidly during XGBoost training on log-transformed fares, and inverse transformation with expm1 produces infinity values that break metric computation.
repair_steps: Replace the unstable objective with reg:squarederror for log-fare regression.
Monitor validation RMSE and enable early stopping so training terminates when held-out performance stops improving.
Use the best validated boosting iteration for validation and test inference.
Check predictions for finiteness and clip log-scale outputs to a fare-appropriate finite range before applying expm1.
After inverse transformation, verify that all predictions are finite before calculating RMSE or passing predictions to a residual model.
repairs.root_cause: An unstable regression objective and unconstrained boosting produce extreme log-scale predictions; exponentiating those predictions overflows floating-point range.
repairs.title: Provisional: Stabilize log-fare boosting before inverse transformation
repairs.when_to_use: Use when XGBoost log-target training shows rapidly increasing validation RMSE or when expm1 of model outputs yields infinity or non-finite fare predictions.

repairs.failure_pattern: Training succeeds, but validation crashes with CUDA out-of-memory when the complete multi-million-row validation matrix is passed through the neural network in one forward call.
repair_steps: Wrap validation features in a DataLoader or equivalent bounded batch iterator.
Run validation under evaluation mode and a no-gradient or inference context.
Move one validation batch at a time to the GPU and release batch-local tensors after accumulating metric statistics.
Accumulate squared-error sums and observation counts incrementally instead of retaining all validation outputs on the GPU.
Reduce the validation batch size if peak memory remains above the device limit.
repairs.root_cause: A full-partition validation forward pass materializes activations and outputs for millions of taxi rows simultaneously, exceeding GPU memory even though training itself uses manageable mini-batches.
repairs.title: Provisional: Stream neural-network validation through bounded batches
repairs.when_to_use: Use when a neural model trains in mini-batches but evaluates the entire large validation partition in one GPU forward pass and fails during validation with CUDA memory exhaustion.

repairs.failure_pattern: Submission validation reports fewer predictions than test rows because coordinate, passenger-count, or other plausibility filters were applied to the test set.
repair_steps: Apply target and outlier row filtering only to labeled training data.
Retain the original test row count and row order throughout feature engineering and inference.
Convert invalid test inputs into missing or bounded feature values instead of dropping their rows.
Impute non-finite engineered test features using values learned from training data or stable feature-specific defaults.
Build the submission against the original test index or key and assert that its row count and ordering exactly match the original test file.
repairs.root_cause: Training-oriented outlier removal was reused for test preprocessing, deleting required test observations and breaking the one-prediction-per-input-row submission contract.
repairs.title: Confirmed: Preserve every test row while handling invalid feature values
repairs.when_to_use: Use when cleaned test data has fewer rows than the original 9,914-row NYC taxi test set or submission validation reports inconsistent sample counts.
